title: TRA-3945.1 The OTM joint arm has met its seR bar with a NEGATIVE mean and can no longer accrue: rule on which terminal verdict is reachable
description:
Filed from the CFO weekly roll-up TRA-4372 (week ET 2026-09-01..09-07). Pin `f6d72028e403` pid 52 `startedAt 2026-09-04T16:16:52.180Z`, capture `2026-09-08T12:53:07.797Z` off
`/api/health/options-live` and `/api/health/option-journal?rows=all`.

**Pin note:** a foreign deploy landed `668126eed049` pid 77 `startedAt 2026-09-08T12:56:11.028Z`
three minutes after that capture. Every arm statistic below was re-read at `2026-09-08T13:05:07.249Z`
on the NEW pin and is **identical across both builds** (`n 9 / avgR -0.17442 / seR 0.077608 /
netUsd -176.72 / closesRemaining 21 / canAccrue false / verdict null`).

You are named as `verdictOwner` in the window's own record. This is not a request to write the
verdict today -- it is a request to rule on **which verdict is even reachable**, because the window
changed state this week in a way its design did not anticipate.

## What changed

**1. The precision bar is already met, and the mean is negative.**

Served fold, and I replicated it independently from the raw journal rows using the record's own
eligibility + dedupe + clustering rules. Exact match on all four statistics, so the numbers below
are not the route grading itself:

| cut | n | avgR | seR | 95% CI | net $ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| full fold (as served) | 9 | -0.17442 | 0.077608 | [-0.3265, -0.0223] | -176.72 |
| ex hand-close (drop 2 `manual`) | 7 | -0.0913 | 0.0694 | [-0.2273, +0.0446] | -69.48 |
| `profit_lock` only | 5 | +0.0135 | 0.0175 | [-0.0207, +0.0477] | +2.76 |

The pre-registered predicates are `passIf avgR > 0 && seR < 0.10` and
`failIf avgR <= 0 && seR < 0.10`. **seR is already below 0.10 on both cuts** (0.0776 at n=9, 0.0694
at n=7) and avgR is negative on both. The `failIf` arithmetic is satisfied at n=9. The only thing
between this arm and a pre-registered FAIL is `targetCloses: 30`.

**2. n=30 is unreachable.** The record now publishes `cadence.canAccrue: false`,
`cannotAccrueReason: "entry_window_never_intersects_rth"`, `projectedSessionsToTarget: null`,
`closesRemaining: 21`. `OTM_ENTRY_WINDOWS_ET=03:00-03:01` does not intersect 09:30-16:00 ET for
paper or live; `entry_window` blocked 607/607 on 09-02 and 671/671 on 09-03; last `buy_to_open`
09-01. Eleven RTH sessions have elapsed since the 08-23 stamp. **There is no arrival process left
to wait on**, and the un-hold is a board card (`4c364384` on TRA-4217, pending since 09-03, chained
by the CEO recommendation to a second pending card `63a6e493`).

**3. The confound, stated before you rule on it.** The full fold's CI sits entirely below zero, but
that result is carried by the two 2026-09-02 `manual` closes (KO -0.3812, NOK -0.5493, avgR -0.465)
-- the hand-liquidation of the 08-28 `admin` rows. Those are not exits the ruleset chose. Remove
them and the CI straddles zero. **The sign survives on every cut and clears the precision bar on
every cut; what does not survive is the ability to distinguish "negative" from "zero".** A verdict
quoted off the full fold would be quoting a flattening decision as if it were an exit rule.

## What I am asking for

A ruling, on the record, on the terminal disposition of `otm-joint-arm-w1`:

1. **Does `failIf` bind at n=9?** The predicate as written contains no n-floor -- it is
   `avgR <= 0 && seR < 0.10`, and both clauses are true. If the intended reading was
   "evaluated only at n >= targetCloses", say so explicitly, because the record does not say it and
   the next reader will reach the opposite conclusion.
2. **If it does not bind, is `verdict_insufficient_population` correct now, or premature?**
   `verdictWriter.onceOnly: true` -- writing it spends the window. If the board un-holds entries
   next week, a spent window cannot be resumed. Weigh that against leaving `status: "counting"` on a
   window that provably cannot count.
3. **Either way, do not let it sit as `counting`.** `status: "counting"` with
   `canAccrue: false` is a liveness label that is not true. Whatever the ruling, the status should
   say the window is frozen and name the gate.
4. **Rule on the confound handling**: is the graded fold the full n=9, or n=7 ex-hand-close? Please
   pre-register which, before the entry gate re-opens and the sample grows.

## Explicitly out of scope

The arm's own clause is `onFail: REPORT ONLY - drop the arm, do not re-tune`, and I am holding to
it: **no parameter change is proposed or authorized by this ticket.** The window's own
pre-registered caveat ("if the joint arm underperforms, the entry window is the FIRST component to
re-examine") has technically fired, and I am recording that as a fact, not acting on it -- the entry
window is a board flow hold and must not be repaired by an agent.

Full report: TRA-4372 thread and
`_default/tra4372-weekly/TRA-4372-weekly-trading-review-2026-09-08.md`.

ancestors.description:
Weekly trading analisist and readjust/fine tune trading strategies if needed.

--- RESTING DISPOSITION (TRA-1272 rule, enforced by TRA-1646; detector fixed by TRA-1657) -- MANDATORY ON EVERY FIRE, INCLUDING NO-OP FIRES ---
Before this run ends you MUST leave the leaf issue at a valid resting disposition. This is not optional and it is not
satisfied by posting a comment.

STEP 1 -- READ THE BLOCKERS CORRECTLY. This is a trap; get it wrong and you will corrupt a healthy leaf.
  GET /api/issues/{id} returns the blocker list under the key `blockedBy` (array of objects, each with identifier +
  status). The GET response does NOT contain `blockedByIssueIds` -- that key is WRITE-ONLY (it is what you send on a
  PATCH). On a GET it is `undefined` for EVERY issue. Therefore any test of the form "blockedByIssueIds is empty"
  reports zero blockers for every issue in the company, and makes EVERY `blocked` leaf look stranded.
  Do NOT use `blockedByIssueIds` to read. Do NOT substitute `blockerAttention.unresolvedBlockerCount` -- also unreliable.

STEP 2 -- APPLY THE STRAND TEST. The leaf is STRANDED if and only if:
      status == "in_progress"
   OR (status == "blocked" AND no entry in `blockedBy` is still open -- i.e. every blocker is done/cancelled)
  A leaf that is `blocked` WITH at least one still-open `blockedBy` entry is a LEGAL rest under TRA-1272.
  LEAVE IT ALONE. Do not park it, do not comment, do not flip it. Parking a legally-blocked leaf is a wrong PATCH.

STEP 3 -- ONLY IF STRANDED, pick exactly one:
  * Leaf blocks a parent, or is still accruing data toward a gate that has not been met yet
      -> PATCH /api/issues/{id} status: "todo"  (parked-ready. A `todo` leaf STILL counts as an unresolved blocker,
         so the parent stays blocked and nothing is lost by parking it.)
  * Per-fire spawn (originKind: routine_execution) that blocks nothing
      -> PATCH /api/issues/{id} status: "done"  (the routine re-fires and spawns the next instance.)
  * Gate MET / terminal verdict reached
      -> post the verdict, PATCH status: "done", and archive this routine
         (PATCH /api/routines/{id} status: "archived" -- there is no hard delete).

NEVER end a fire with the leaf `in_progress`. If you set status `blocked`, you MUST send first-class blocker ids on the
PATCH via the WRITE key `blockedByIssueIds`, and re-send the COMPLETE list (it replaces, it does not append) -- a
`blocked` leaf whose blocker list is genuinely empty raises a Paperclip `missing_disposition` recovery action that
routes to CFO, burns a heartbeat, and gets re-created on the next fire.
A `request_confirmation` "monitor-rest checkpoint" is NOT a durable rest path: board acceptance CONSUMES the pending
interaction, which removes the review path and re-strands the leaf on the very next fire. Do not rely on one to rest.
--- END RESTING DISPOSITION ---
